papers.title: Plasma proteomic profiles associated with low-dose computed tomography findings and incident lung cancer: a prospective pilot study.
papers.abstract: Plasma proteins may reflect tumor-host biology, but their relationships with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) findings and incident lung cancer remain uncertain. Although LDCT screening has improved survival, challenges remain in risk stratification and interpretation of screening findings. The aim of the present study was to investigate associations between plasma proteomic profiles, LDCT findings and incident lung cancer, and to explore their potential for lung cancer risk stratification.
papers.summary: This prospective pilot study examined whether plasma protein profiles are associated with low-dose CT (LDCT) screening findings and the subsequent development of lung cancer. The authors aimed to see if proteomic data could help stratify lung cancer risk beyond what LDCT alone provides. As a pilot study, it primarily establishes feasibility and preliminary associations rather than definitive clinical utility.

papers.title: Identification of hepatitis B virus-associated membrane proteins as prognostic biomarkers for hepatocellular carcinoma based on retrospective analysis of integrated membrane proteomics.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is one of the major risk factors for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development. Current prognostic assessment of HBV-associated HCC (HBV-HCC) largely relies on clinicopathological parameters, such as tumor stage, liver function, and serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels, which have limited accuracy in identifying patients at high risk of recurrence or poor survival. Therefore, reliable molecular biomarkers are urgently needed to improve individualized risk stratification and guide postoperative surveillance and therapeutic decision-making. HBV infection induce
papers.summary: This study integrates membrane proteomics data to identify HBV-associated membrane proteins that could serve as prognostic biomarkers for hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors retrospectively analyzed patient samples to find membrane protein signatures linked to recurrence or survival outcomes in HBV-HCC. These candidate biomarkers may improve risk stratification beyond conventional clinicopathological parameters like tumor stage and AFP levels.

papers.title: Analysis and validation of prognostic markers for thyroid cancer by single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Thyroid cancer represents the most prevalent malignancy within the endocrine system, exhibiting consistent increasing incidence rates over the years. We aim to utilize single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset to analyze key genes associated with prognosis in thyroid cancer.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to identify genes associated with prognosis in thyroid cancer. The authors analyze cell-type-specific expression patterns to nominate prognostic markers, which are then validated in bulk transcriptomic cohorts. The work aims to provide candidate biomarkers for improved risk stratification in thyroid cancer.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and radiomics in small cell lung cancer: a narrative review of imaging and multisource data integration.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and radiomics are increasingly used to analyze imaging and multisource data in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the directness and clinical maturity of the available evidence remain uncertain. This narrative review aimed to summarize and critically evaluate SCLC-specific, mixed-cohort, and indirect evidence across diagnostic classification, prognostic prediction, treatment-associated outcomes, and lesion segmentation.
papers.summary: This narrative review critically evaluates the current evidence on AI and radiomics applications in small cell lung cancer, covering diagnostic classification, prognosis prediction, treatment outcomes, and lesion segmentation. It highlights that much of the available evidence is indirect or from mixed-cohort studies, and that clinical maturity remains uncertain, underscoring the need for more SCLC-specific validation.

papers.title: Biological rationales from language models enable leakage-resistant forecasts of target-indication success.
papers.abstract: Identifying which target-indication (T-I) hypotheses can translate into clinical success remains a central challenge in drug discovery. We present PRIORITI (Prospective Rationale-Informed Outcome Reasoning for Integrated Target-indication Intelligence), a leakage-resistant framework that separates upstream biological evidence synthesis from outcome prediction. Given only a target gene and disease indication, a domain-instructed large language model (LLM) synthesizes drug-agnostic human genetics across prespecified channels. These evidence were embedded and combined with static entity context d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present PRIORITI, a framework that uses a domain-instructed large language model to synthesize drug-agnostic biological evidence for a given target-indication pair, then predicts clinical success from these rationales in a leakage-resistant manner. By separating upstream evidence synthesis from outcome prediction, the approach aims to avoid data leakage that can inflate performance in target-indication forecasting. This offers a new strategy for prioritizing drug targets with better generalization to prospective settings.

papers.title: AI-Based Comparison of UniProt annotations and Literature Across Human Kinases.
papers.abstract: Curated protein records and their supporting publications organize biological evidence at different levels of detail. Here, we used AI to independently answer a set of biological questions using either UniProt records or the full texts of the literature cited by those records, and then used AI-based evaluation to compare the resulting answers in terms of information coverage and semantic agreement. Fifty human proteins were selected from ten groups in a kinase sequence collection. Target-identity filtering retained 1,749 protein-publication records representing 1,655 distinct publications. For
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint uses AI to compare the information content of UniProt protein records against the full texts of the publications they cite, focusing on 50 human kinases. The authors generated answers to biological questions from each source and used AI-based evaluation to assess coverage and semantic agreement, finding differences in how much and what kind of information each source provides. The work suggests that curated database records and primary literature are complementary rather than redundant sources of biological knowledge.

papers.title: Transformer-based decision support with CNN and ViT for prognostic risk stratification following adjuvant chemotherapy in high-grade glioma: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) exhibit marked intratumoral heterogeneity, which is associated with variable survival outcomes among patients receiving standard adjuvant chemotherapy. Conventional methods relying on molecular biomarkers are constrained by technical limitations and tumor heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop a multi-channel 2.5D deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) features to noninvasively stratify HGG patients based on expected survival outcomes following postoperative adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) chemotherapy a
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This study develops a multi-channel 2.5D deep learning framework combining CNN and Vision Transformer features to noninvasively stratify high-grade glioma patients by expected survival after adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy. The approach aims to overcome limitations of molecular biomarkers, which are constrained by technical issues and tumor heterogeneity, using multicenter imaging data.

papers.title: CheckAMG: Accurate Identification of Auxiliary Viral Genes with Genome-Language Models.
papers.abstract: Viruses shape microbial metabolism through auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) that reprogram host metabolism, physiology, and gene regulation during infection. Identifying AVGs is complicated by ambiguous viral versus cellular assignment, inconsistent curation, and reliance on sequence homology that misses divergent functions. Here we present CheckAMG, which pairs annotation-based AVG prediction, curated with a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic function, with a finetuned genome-language model for annotation-independent discovery. Benchmarked against DRAM-V and VIBRAN
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CheckAMG is a new tool that identifies auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) by combining annotation-based prediction with a fine-tuned genome-language model, addressing the difficulty of distinguishing viral from cellular genes and detecting divergent functions missed by homology-based methods. It uses a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic functions, and is benchmarked against existing tools DRAM-V and VIBRANT.

papers.title: DeepNPA: A protBert-based framework for residue-level annotation of neuropeptide precursors.
papers.abstract: Neuropeptides are key signaling molecules that regulate the nervous and endocrine systems, and their maturation depends on precise proteolytic cleavage of precursor proteins. However, residue-level annotation remains essential yet experimentally labor intensive, with limited dedicated computational tools. Here, we present DeepNPA, a residue-level annotation framework that integrates ProtBert, a pretrained protein language model, with focal loss for imbalance-aware optimization. DeepNPA was trained and evaluated on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset annotated using the BIO scheme. On a
papers.summary: DeepNPA is a new computational framework that uses the pretrained protein language model ProtBert, combined with focal loss to handle class imbalance, to annotate neuropeptide precursor proteins at the residue level. It was trained and evaluated on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset using the BIO annotation scheme, aiming to replace labor-intensive experimental annotation of neuropeptide cleavage sites.

papers.title: Dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding for anticancer peptide prediction via transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Computational identification of anti-tumor peptides (ACPs) is challenged by limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences. Standard transformer positional encodings fail to capture the periodicities and local motifs that govern peptide function. We propose dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), which replaces fixed sinusoidal encodings with parallel adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches, fused by a context-aware gating mechanism. A dual-stage transfer learning strategy pre-trains on 5,785 curated peptide sequences before fine-tuning on ACP74
papers.summary: The authors introduce dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), a transformer positional encoding scheme that combines adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches via context-aware gating to better capture periodicities and local motifs in peptide sequences. Using a dual-stage transfer learning strategy, they pre-train on 5,785 curated peptides and fine-tune for anticancer peptide prediction, addressing limited training data and multi-scale sequence features.

papers.title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from mult
papers.summary: The authors present SF-DTI, a deep learning framework for predicting drug-target interactions that combines multiple protein encoders, aligns drug structure with semantic representations, and progressively refines cross-modal features. The approach aims to bridge the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein data while leveraging complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders.

papers.title: Machine learning and multi-omics analyses reveal CLDN1 as a candidate marker associated with colorectal cancer invasion and nutlin-3a (-) response.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is molecularly, cellularly and spatially heterogeneous, and current staging systems and biomarkers incompletely explain prognosis and treatment response. This study integrated transcriptomics, machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics and in vitro experiments to prioritize candidate CRC-associated markers and characterize their potential biological and clinical relevance.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and in vitro experiments to identify candidate markers associated with colorectal cancer invasion and response to the drug nutlin-3a. CLDN1 emerged as a top candidate marker linked to tumor invasion and negative nutlin-3a response, suggesting it may have prognostic or predictive value in CRC.

papers.title: Quantifying the impact of genetic mutations on enhancer dynamics.
papers.abstract: Transcriptional regulation is mediated by enhancers, yet how genetic perturbations alter enhancer activity and gene expression remains unclear. We develop UDI-UMI-STARR-seq, integrating dual indexes and unique molecular identifiers, and combine it with RNA-seq to profile perturbation-associated changes in enhancer activity and gene expression. We apply this approach to 253,632 fragments representing 46,142 cell type-specific candidate enhancers and assess the impact of CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of six transcription factors (ATF2, CTCF, FOXA1, LEF1, TCF7L2, and SCRT1). We identify responsiv
papers.summary: The authors developed UDI-UMI-STARR-seq, a new method combining dual indexes and unique molecular identifiers with RNA-seq to measure how genetic perturbations affect enhancer activity and gene expression. Applying this to over 250,000 enhancer fragments and CRISPR deletion of six transcription factors, they identified enhancers responsive to specific regulators. This provides a scalable framework for linking transcription factor perturbations to enhancer dynamics.

papers.title: PTGS2/COX-2 is associated with neurovascular and blood-brain barrier changes in behaviourally classified MRL/lpr mice.
papers.abstract: To identify candidate genes of interest in neuropsychiatric SLE (NPSLE) through integrated transcriptomic and machine-learning analysis, and to investigate the association of prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2)/cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) with neurovascular unit changes and blood–brain barrier (BBB) disruption in behaviourally classified MRL/lpr mice.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with machine-learning analysis to identify candidate genes involved in neuropsychiatric lupus (NPSLE), highlighting PTGS2/COX-2 as a key gene. Using behaviourally classified MRL/lpr mice, the authors show that PTGS2/COX-2 is associated with changes in the neurovascular unit and disruption of the blood-brain barrier, suggesting a potential mechanistic and therapeutic target for NPSLE.

papers.title: Network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell analysis, and molecular docking reveal 6PPD/6PPD-Q-associated atrial fibrillation signatures.
papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent sustained arrhythmia worldwide, and environmental factors are increasingly recognized as contributors to its complex pathogenesis. The tire antioxidant N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its oxidation product 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) are emerging environmental contaminants with reported cardiotoxicity; however, their molecular relationship with AF remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell analysis, and molecular docking to investigate how the tire-derived contaminants 6PPD and 6PPD-Q may contribute to atrial fibrillation. The authors identify molecular signatures and potential mechanisms linking these environmental pollutants to AF pathogenesis, suggesting a previously unrecognized environmental risk factor for the arrhythmia.

papers.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of Novel STK3/4 Inhibitors with Anti-Obesity Potential.
papers.abstract: Obesity is associated with impaired adipocyte metabolism driven in part by mitochondrial dysfunction. Serine/threonine-protein kinase 3 (STK3) and STK4 promote mitophagy, leading to reduced mitochondrial mass in adipose tissue. Thus, inhibition of STK3/4 represents a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity and related metabolic disorders.
papers.summary: This study develops and preclinically evaluates novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting STK3/4 kinases, which promote mitophagy and reduce mitochondrial mass in adipose tissue. By blocking these kinases, the inhibitors aim to restore mitochondrial function in adipocytes and combat obesity and related metabolic disorders.

papers.title: PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal-Binding Site and Type Prediction.
papers.abstract: Metal binding to proteins is crucial for many biological functions, yet the prediction of metal-binding sites and metal types remains underexplored compared to other biomolecular interactions. Despite advances in deep learning, computational methods have achieved limited success in this area; even the best-reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy on high-resolution crystal structures, and even worse when applied to medium-resolution data. We hypothesize that the main challenge lies in the nature of metal binding. While the putative sites span the entire protein surface, ac
papers.summary: PrOMet is a new deep learning method for predicting where metals bind on proteins and which metal type binds there. It addresses a gap in the field, since existing tools perform only moderately well, especially on lower-resolution structures. The approach aims to improve both accuracy and robustness for this underexplored prediction task.

papers.title: Epigenetic Silencing of CYYR1 Promotes Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression Through TRIM21-Dependent Regulation of HMMR Stability.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Integrative multi-omics and machine-learning analyses across independent cohorts identified CYYR1 as a frequently downregulated transmembrane protein in LUAD, with low expression associated with poor prognosis and promoter hypermethylation. CYYR1 restoration suppressed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, tumor growth, and metastasis. Mechanistically, CYYR1 facilitated TRIM21-dependent ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of HMMR, thereby reducing CDC20-associated oncogenic signaling. Biochemical and
papers.summary: This study identifies CYYR1 as a transmembrane protein that is frequently silenced by promoter hypermethylation in lung adenocarcinoma, with low expression linked to poor patient prognosis. Restoring CYYR1 suppresses tumor growth and metastasis by promoting TRIM21-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of HMMR, which in turn reduces CDC20-associated oncogenic signaling.

papers.title: AI Model Reporting Standards in Health Care: Systematic Review and Consolidation.
papers.abstract: AI technologies are currently experiencing significant growth in development and use in health care. The AI model lifecycle includes several stages, all of which should be adequately described. Reporting standards are commonly used for this purpose. However, the plain-text structure of these standards prevents transparent machine-readability of this information.
papers.summary: This systematic review consolidates existing AI model reporting standards in health care and addresses their limitation of being plain-text and not machine-readable. The authors propose a consolidated, machine-readable framework to improve transparency and interoperability of AI model documentation across the lifecycle.

papers.title: Massively Multiplexed Photonic Chip With Cross-Channel Fusion For Harmonized Biosensing.
papers.abstract: Accurate, label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures is limited by poor multiplexing scalability and inconsistent responses across sensor samples. We introduce a transformative sensing platform that integrates large-scale photonic multiplexing with data-driven analytics to overcome these constraints. Our modular, affordable glass-chip whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) photonic architecture is designed to support simultaneous readout of up to 100 sensing channels comprising over 10 000 high-Q microresonators, exceeding existing multiplexing capabilities by more than two orders of magnitude.
papers.summary: The authors present a glass-chip photonic sensing platform based on whispering-gallery-mode microresonators that can simultaneously read out up to 100 sensing channels containing over 10,000 high-Q resonators, a multiplexing scale roughly two orders of magnitude beyond existing biosensors. They pair this hardware with data-driven cross-channel fusion analytics to harmonize inconsistent sensor responses, enabling accurate label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures.

papers.title: A self-supervised foundation model for large-scale zebrafish image analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput zebrafish screening generates large volumes of imaging data, creating a need for scalable computational methods that reduce dependence on manual annotation and repeated task-specific model development. In this study, we develop a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis pretrained on more than 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous zebrafish imaging datasets spanning different developmental stages, imaging platforms, modalities, and experimental conditions. By learning a shared representation from diverse unlabeled zebrafish images, the proposed framework
papers.summary: This paper presents a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis, pretrained on over 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous zebrafish imaging datasets covering different developmental stages, platforms, and modalities. The approach learns a shared representation from unlabeled images, reducing the need for manual annotation and task-specific model development in high-throughput zebrafish screening.

papers.title: ParaEM: Antigen-aware sequence-based paratope prediction with Expectation-Maximization.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of antibody paratopes-the residues contacting the antigen-is vital for understanding antibody-antigen recognition, antibody engineering, and vaccine design. However, structure-based predictors require antibody structural inputs, which are often obtained from experimentally determined antibody-antigen complexes in benchmark settings but are generally unavailable for new sequences. Conversely, sequence-based predictors scale efficiently but remain largely antigen-agnostic, limiting their use of pair-specific antigen context.
papers.summary: ParaEM is a new computational method that predicts antibody paratope residues directly from sequence, while incorporating antigen context through an Expectation-Maximization framework. This addresses a key limitation of prior sequence-based predictors, which were largely antigen-agnostic and thus unable to exploit pair-specific antigen information. The approach aims to improve paratope prediction for antibody engineering and vaccine design without requiring antibody structures.

papers.title: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning.
papers.abstract: Proteins are the main drivers of cell function and disease, making proteomics a powerful technique for biomarker discovery and defining cell identity. While current technologies can profile thousands of proteins and reach single-cell sensitivity, limited throughput restricts applications such as robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts. To close this gap, we present a deep-learning (DL) approach for the direct analysis of mass spectrometric (MS) data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identity. Specifically, we introduce the ProFormer, a transformer pipeline that clas
papers.summary: ProFormer is a transformer-based deep learning pipeline that directly classifies mass spectrometry proteomic profiles, assigning samples to their biological or clinical identity without requiring extensive preprocessing. It is designed to work on both single-cell and plasma proteomes, addressing throughput limitations in large cohort classification tasks.

papers.title: pLM-HP: Peptide hormone prediction using pre-trained protein language model representations.
papers.abstract: Peptide hormones play key roles in metabolic regulation, growth and development, and the maintenance of homeostasis and are important targets for drug discovery and design. However, traditional experimental methods for screening and identifying peptide hormones are costly and inefficient. Although existing machine learning methods have made some progress, they pay limited attention to class imbalance, and there is still room to improve prediction performance.
papers.summary: The authors present pLM-HP, a machine-learning method that uses representations from a pre-trained protein language model to predict peptide hormones, explicitly addressing class imbalance to improve performance over prior approaches. This offers a faster, cheaper computational alternative to costly experimental screening for peptide hormone discovery.

papers.title: Multi-objective-conditioned-return-blocks decision transformer: a novel approach for multi-objective de novo drug design.
papers.abstract: Designing novel molecules that simultaneously satisfy several, often conflicting, properties is a long-standing challenge in drug design. While recent deep learning advances optimize single targets effectively, navigating the tradeoffs required for multiple objectives remains a difficult problem.
papers.summary: The paper introduces the Multi-Objective-Conditioned-Return-Blocks Decision Transformer (MOC-RB-DT), a novel deep learning architecture for de novo drug design that can generate molecules satisfying multiple, often conflicting, objectives simultaneously. It extends the decision transformer framework with return blocks conditioned on multiple objectives, enabling flexible tradeoff navigation during molecular generation. This addresses a key limitation of existing methods that typically optimize only a single target property.

papers.title: Identification of Mitochondrial Dynamics-Related Genes as Diagnostic Biomarkers for Osteoarthritis Using Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis and Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, painful joint disease whose early diagnosis is critical for effective treatment. Since mitochondrial dynamics have been implicated in the onset and progression of OA, this study aimed to explore the diagnostic value of mitochondrial dynamics-related genes (MDRGs) in OA.
papers.summary: This study applies weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to identify mitochondrial dynamics-related genes as potential diagnostic biomarkers for osteoarthritis. The authors aim to leverage the link between mitochondrial dysfunction and OA pathogenesis to improve early diagnosis. The work represents a bioinformatics-driven biomarker discovery effort in a common joint disease.

papers.title: CatRange enables robust prediction of enzyme variant kinetic regimes.
papers.abstract: Predicting enzyme kinetics directly from sequence remains a central challenge in computational biology, particularly for mutations at catalytically essential residues. Existing models often default to wild-type predictions even when mutations cause substantial activity loss. This limits their utility for enzyme design and mechanistic inference. Here, we introduce CatRange, a machine learning framework trained on CatLog-27k, a human-in-the-loop, AI-agent curated dataset of 27,176 in vitro enzyme-substrate kinetic records. CatLog-27k was created through systematic audit and correction of BRENDA
papers.summary: CatRange is a machine learning framework that predicts enzyme kinetic regimes directly from sequence, trained on CatLog-27k, a human-in-the-loop AI-agent curated dataset of 27,176 in vitro enzyme-substrate kinetic records derived from systematic audit and correction of BRENDA. The work addresses a key failure mode of existing models, which often default to wild-type predictions even when mutations at catalytically essential residues cause substantial activity loss, thereby improving utility for enzyme design and mechanistic inference.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Identification of Madecassoside as a Potential RAD51 Modulator That Sensitizes Breast Cancer Cells to Cisplatin.
papers.abstract: Homologous recombination (HR) is an essential pathway for preserving the genomic stability of cells by repairing DNA damage, especially double-strand breaks and interstrand crosslinks. RAD51 recombinase plays a central role in the HR pathway, and when DNA damage occurs, RAD51 binds to single-stranded DNA at the cleavage site to form a helical nucleoprotein filament. Therefore, pharmacological inhibition of RAD51 is emerging as an attractive strategy to block the repair mechanisms of cancer cells and maximize the therapeutic efficacy of conventional radiation and chemotherapy. Several RAD51 sma
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to screen for compounds that modulate RAD51, a key protein in DNA repair, and identifies madecassoside as a potential inhibitor. Madecassoside sensitizes breast cancer cells to cisplatin, suggesting it could enhance chemotherapy effectiveness by blocking DNA repair.

papers.title: Moran's index habitat and peritumoral radiomics based on digital breast tomosynthesis for predicting Ki-67 status in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: The heterogeneity of breast cancer is a key factor influencing treatment decisions and patient prognosis. As a crucial cell proliferation marker, the expression level of the Ki-67 protein is closely associated with tumor aggressiveness, recurrence risk, and prognosis. The goal of this study was to develop and validate an integrated radiomics model based on digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) that incorporates both habitat subregions and peritumoral features to preoperatively predict Ki-67 expression status in breast cancer.
papers.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
papers.summary: This study developed a radiomics model using digital breast tomosynthesis imaging that combines habitat subregion analysis (via Moran's index) with peritumoral features to predict Ki-67 expression status in breast cancer preoperatively. The integrated model aims to non-invasively assess tumor proliferation marker status, which is linked to cancer aggressiveness and prognosis.

papers.title: Empathy in the Soil, Agents on the Desktop: Why Plant Pathology Needs a Scientist-in-the-Loop AI Paradigm.
papers.abstract: Plant pathology faces a cognitive bottleneck caused by the growing volume of biological data. Addressing it requires a shift from passive chatbots to autonomous AI research agents that operate in Goal-Action-State cycles. Researchers can set up a local, desktop-based agentic framework that combines semantic discovery, LLM-Wiki knowledge synthesis, and in silico prevalidation, managed under a human-directed three-tier organizational model. Strict "Scientist-in-the-Loop" boundaries, which means that a human researcher sets the goals, reviews AI-generated output before it is treated as evidence,
papers.summary: This perspective article argues that plant pathology is constrained by a cognitive bottleneck from expanding biological data, and proposes shifting from passive chatbots to autonomous AI research agents that operate in Goal-Action-State cycles. The authors outline a local, desktop-based agentic framework combining semantic discovery, LLM-Wiki knowledge synthesis, and in silico prevalidation, governed by a human-directed three-tier model with strict Scientist-in-the-Loop boundaries.

papers.title: Omics data discovery agents: Agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data.
papers.abstract: The biomedical literature contains a vast collection of omics studies, yet most published data remain functionally inaccessible for computational reuse. When raw data are deposited in public repositories, essential information for reproducing reported results is dispersed across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and in the rarer cases where intermediate data (e.g., protein abundance files) are shared, their location is irregular. Here we present an agentic framework for the agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data. The system employs lar
papers.summary: The authors present an agentic framework that uses LLM-based agents to retrieve, reanalyze, and synthesize published omics data from the biomedical literature. The system addresses the problem that most published omics data remain functionally inaccessible because key information is scattered across main text, supplements, and code repositories. It aims to make published omics studies computationally reusable by automating the discovery and integration of dispersed data.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of mitochondrial proteomes across the tree of life.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria arose from the endosymbiosis of a bacterium with an archaea-related host cell about 2 billion years ago. To understand their origins and evolution, we compared experimentally defined mitoproteomes from the MitoCarta Tree of Life project. Across eight organisms, we identified 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins within 3,199 families, of which 43% lack Pfam domains. We report 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens yet absent in humans, representing promising candidate targets for protozoan infectious diseases. Leveraging our experimentally defined mitoproteomes, we
papers.summary: This study compares experimentally defined mitochondrial proteomes across eight organisms spanning the tree of life, identifying 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins in 3,199 families, 43% of which lack known Pfam domains. The authors highlight 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens but absent in humans, offering potential drug targets for protozoan infectious diseases.

papers.title: Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health challenge, leading to substantial mortality and economic losses without science-based interventions. Conventional approaches to combating AMR have important limitations in addressing this escalating threat. Recent advances in AI, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, provide new opportunities to integrate multimodal data for AMR research. However, evidence remains uneven, with many approaches limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation. Here, we critically review AI
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, can integrate multimodal data to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights that while these approaches show promise, most evidence remains limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation.

papers.title: Multimodal biomarkers and prediction models for stricturing and penetrating progression in Crohn's disease.
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease can progress from non-stricturing, non-penetrating inflammation (B1) to stricturing (B2) or penetrating (B3) complications, yet risk is commonly recognized only after structural damage is established. This narrative review examines clinical, endoscopic, genomic, circulating, stool, tissue, imaging, radiomic, and computational biomarkers relevant to behavioral-progression risk and separates direct B1-to-B2 or source-defined B3 evidence from related prognostic and mechanistic evidence, while distinguishing internal penetrating from perianal fistulizing disease when source reporti
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys clinical, endoscopic, genomic, circulating, stool, tissue, imaging, radiomic, and computational biomarkers that may predict progression of Crohn's disease from inflammatory (B1) to stricturing (B2) or penetrating (B3) phenotypes. It emphasizes distinguishing direct B1-to-B2/B3 evidence from broader prognostic signals and separating internal penetrating from perianal fistulizing disease. The review aims to inform multimodal prediction models for earlier risk stratification before structural damage occurs.

papers.title: A dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework for exploratory classification of colorectal cancer histopathology and hepatocellular carcinoma clinical records.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain major diagnostic challenges because classification often depends on modality-specific evidence that is stored in separate public datasets. This study evaluates a dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework using two independent and unpaired data sources: colorectal histopathological image patches and structured HCC clinical-biochemical records. The study is therefore positioned as an exploratory investigation of representation learning across heterogeneous medical datasets. The CNN branch extracts spatial and glandular texture features from
papers.summary: This exploratory study applies a dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework to two unrelated datasets: colorectal cancer histopathology images and hepatocellular carcinoma clinical-biochemical records. The CNN branch learns spatial texture features from image patches while the LSTM branch handles structured clinical data, testing whether a shared architecture can perform representation learning across heterogeneous, unpaired medical sources. The work is framed as a proof-of-concept rather than a validated diagnostic tool.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning models to predict venous thromboembolism in sepsis patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Sepsis patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) face a substantially elevated risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet prediction tools tailored for this population are lacking. This study aimed to develop and validate interpretable machine learning models for predicting in-hospital VTE in septic patients with T2DM.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates interpretable machine learning models to predict in-hospital venous thromboembolism (VTE) in sepsis patients who also have type 2 diabetes mellitus, a group at elevated VTE risk with no existing tailored prediction tools. The work addresses a clinical gap by combining predictive modeling with interpretability for a specific high-risk patient population.

papers.title: Lab to codes: multimodel advanced AI-driven pipelines to drive antimicrobial peptide design for the post-antibiotic era.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has outpaced the development of new antimicrobial agents, necessitating transformative approaches such as AI-driven in-silico drug discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising alternatives due to their broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and limited susceptibility to resistance. However, the transition from bench to bedside remains constrained by certain challenges, such as instability, potency, and cytotoxicity. Here, well-integrated, multi-model AI-driven pipeline strategies for the mining and discovery of novel AMPs are
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrated multi-model AI pipelines can accelerate the discovery and design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights how AI-driven in-silico approaches help overcome key bottlenecks such as peptide instability, potency, and cytotoxicity that hinder the translation of AMPs from bench to bedside.

papers.title: Association between insulin resistance-related indices and cardiovascular disease in patients with atopic dermatitis: mutual validation using real-world and NHANES data.
papers.abstract: The number of patients with atopic dermatitis (AD) who develop cardiovascular disease (CVD) has been increasing year by year. However, reliable biomarkers for identifying AD patients with a higher burden of prevalent CVD remain lacking.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether insulin resistance-related indices can serve as biomarkers for identifying atopic dermatitis (AD) patients at higher risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Using both real-world clinical data and NHANES survey data, the authors mutually validate the association between these metabolic indices and prevalent CVD in AD patients. The findings suggest that insulin resistance indices may help stratify cardiovascular risk in this population.

papers.title: Multi-scale Gaussian product-of-experts for missing sequence multiple sclerosis lesion segmentation.
papers.abstract: To develop and evaluate a unified framework for multiple sclerosis (MS) white matter lesion segmentation that operates robustly under clinically prevalent missing sequence magnetic resonance imaging conditions.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a multi-scale Gaussian product-of-experts framework for segmenting multiple sclerosis white matter lesions from MRI, designed to remain robust when some MRI sequences are missing—a common clinical scenario. The approach aims to provide reliable lesion segmentation without requiring complete multi-sequence acquisitions.

papers.title: Identification of Crohn's disease-associated molecular signatures by integrative bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with rising global incidence. Its multifactorial etiology involves genetic, environmental, microbial, and immunological factors. Current diagnostic methods are invasive and costly, underscoring the need for improved biomarkers and non-invasive tools for early detection and monitoring.
papers.summary: This study applies integrative bioinformatics to identify molecular signatures associated with Crohn's disease, aiming to uncover candidate biomarkers that could improve on current invasive and costly diagnostic approaches. The authors combine computational analysis of public datasets with experimental validation to confirm key findings. The work contributes to the search for non-invasive diagnostic and monitoring tools for this chronic inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Emergence of OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae ST5994, a sister lineage of the high-risk ST307 clone.
papers.abstract: Carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (CP-KP) represents a major public health threat. The global dissemination of antimicrobial resistance is largely driven by high-risk clones (HRCs), such as ST307/OXA-48, ST11/OXA-48 and ST512/KPC-3, which currently dominate the epidemiology of CP-KP in Spain. This study aimed to describe the emergence, dissemination and genomic evolution of an OXA-48-producing K. pneumoniae ST5994 clone in Cantabria, Spain, and to characterize its genomic, phenotypic and epidemiological features.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes a newly emerging OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae clone, ST5994, in Cantabria, Spain, which is a sister lineage to the globally disseminated high-risk ST307 clone. Through genomic, phenotypic, and epidemiological analyses, the authors describe its emergence and dissemination, highlighting its potential to become a new public health concern given its close relationship to a major high-risk clone.

papers.title: Early prediction of 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke: an explainable model based on routine clinical data.
papers.abstract: Accurate early prediction of 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke is essential for prognostic communication, early management planning, and resource allocation. However, clinically applicable and interpretable prediction tools based on routinely collected data remain limited.
papers.summary: This study develops an explainable machine learning model that predicts 3-month functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke using only routine clinical data collected early after admission. The model aims to support prognostic communication and early management planning while remaining interpretable for clinical use.

papers.title: Association between dietary branched-chain amino acid intake and anaemia risk in children and adolescents: a matched case-control study.
papers.abstract: Anaemia in children and adolescents is multifactorial, and evidence on dietary amino-acid intake in relation to anaemia remains limited. This study examined the association between dietary branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) intake and haemoglobin (Hb)-defined anaemia among Chinese children and adolescents using data from the 2016-2019 China Children and Lactating Women Nutrition and Health Survey. Among 11,134 eligible participants aged 6-17 years, quantile g-computation and the Boruta algorithm were first used to screen 20 dietary amino acids. A 1:4 propensity score-matched sample was then cons
papers.summary: This matched case-control study analyzed dietary data from over 11,000 Chinese children and adolescents to examine whether branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) intake is associated with anemia risk. Using quantile g-computation and the Boruta algorithm to screen 20 dietary amino acids, the authors identified BCAA intake as a potential dietary factor linked to hemoglobin-defined anemia. The findings suggest that dietary amino acid composition may play a role in childhood anemia risk, though the observational design limits causal inference.

papers.title: Immune-related molecular links between asthma and Alzheimer's disease identified by multi-omics, machine learning and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: Epidemiological evidence suggests that asthma increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet their shared immune-related molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify immune-associated molecular links between the two diseases.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data, machine learning, and single-cell analysis to uncover shared immune-related molecular mechanisms linking asthma and Alzheimer's disease. It identifies candidate immune genes and pathways that may explain the epidemiological association between the two conditions, offering potential targets for further investigation.

papers.title: Association and discriminative value of insulin resistance surrogate markers for aortic stiffness in asymptomatic adults.
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance surrogate markers, including the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, TyG-BMI, and TG/HDL-C ratio, have been associated with aortic stiffness in high-risk populations. Their comparative associations and incremental discrimination in asymptomatic adults remain unclear. We therefore compared these markers and evaluated a simplified model for cfPWV-defined aortic stiffness.
papers.summary: This study compares three insulin resistance surrogate markers (TyG index, TyG-BMI, and TG/HDL-C ratio) for their association with aortic stiffness, measured by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV), in asymptomatic adults. It also evaluates whether a simplified model using these markers can improve discrimination of aortic stiffness beyond traditional risk factors.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of graph neural networks and classical machine learning for carbapenem-resistance prediction and genomic interpretation in Acinetobacter baumannii.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii is a hospital-associated pathogen linked to high mortality and limited treatment options. Although many resistance determinants have been identified, how they organize into coordinated systems remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study compares graph neural networks with classical machine learning methods for predicting carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii, a major hospital-associated pathogen. It also explores how these models can aid in interpreting the genomic organization of resistance determinants, moving beyond simple gene presence/absence toward understanding coordinated resistance systems.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning characterize LTA4H-linked lipid metabolism and inflammatory signatures in the knee osteoarthritis IPFP/synovium compartment.
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a whole-joint disease characterized by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and metabolic imbalance. To define lipid metabolism-related transcriptional heterogeneity within the infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP)/synovium compartment, we integrated publicly available single-cell transcriptomic data from IPFP/synovium-derived joint cells with bulk synovial transcriptomic datasets from patients with KOA and controls. Lipid metabolism-related scores were derived using multiple single-cell scoring algorithms, and candidate genes were identified through score-associated analyse
papers.summary: This study integrates public single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data from knee osteoarthritis patients to characterize lipid metabolism-related transcriptional heterogeneity in the infrapatellar fat pad/synovium compartment. Using multiple single-cell scoring algorithms and machine learning, the authors identify LTA4H-linked lipid metabolism and inflammatory signatures as candidate features of KOA pathology.

papers.title: Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener.
papers.abstract: Thermostability limits the use of sweet proteins as sugar substitutes in thermally processed foods. Here, we report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a recently identified fungal sweet protein with low intrinsic stability. We determined the HTS crystal structure and used it to guide subsequent computational analyses. Rosetta and ThermoMPNN evaluated candidate substitutions from complementary physics-based and deep-learning-based perspectives, and the selected single-mutant library was experimentally characterized. The resulting melti
papers.summary: The study presents a computation-guided workflow to improve the thermostability of Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a fungal sweet protein with poor intrinsic stability that limits its use in processed foods. Using the newly solved HTS crystal structure, the authors combined Rosetta (physics-based) and ThermoMPNN (deep-learning) predictions to design single-mutant variants, which were then experimentally tested for improved melting temperatures. This demonstrates an integrated structure-based strategy for engineering stable sweet proteins as sugar substitutes.

papers.title: Characterization and clustering of immunocompetent proteins based on ESM-2 sequence embedding and physicochemical feature fusion.
papers.abstract: Traditional sequence-comparison methods face challenges when classifying and identifying low-homology proteins formed by convergent evolution. In this exploratory study, we built a PCA-based unsupervised clustering workflow combining high-dimensional embeddings from the frozen pre-trained protein-language model ESM-2 and weighted-fused physicochemical features. The workflow was explored for family-level grouping, identification of putative functional conservation, and cross-species evolutionary analysis of immune-active proteins. An independent external test dataset was further used to prelimi
papers.summary: This exploratory study combines ESM-2 protein language model embeddings with physicochemical features in a PCA-based unsupervised clustering workflow to group immunocompetent proteins, including low-homology proteins that traditional sequence comparison struggles to classify. The authors use this approach for family-level grouping, detecting putative functional conservation, and cross-species evolutionary analysis, with preliminary validation on an external test dataset.

papers.title: RCSB PDB AI Help Desk: retrieval-augmented generation for protein structure deposition support.
papers.abstract: Structural biologists have contributed more than 260 000 experimentally determined three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules to the Protein Data Bank. Incoming depositions are validated and biocurated by approximately 20 expert biocurators at the collaborating data centers worldwide. Biocurators at the Research Collaboratory for Structural Bioinformatics Protein Data Bank, who process more than 40% of global depositions, face growing difficulty sustaining efficient Help Desk operations, having received roughly 19 000 depositor messages across some 8000 entries in 2025.
papers.summary: The RCSB PDB has developed an AI Help Desk that uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to assist structural biologists depositing new structures into the Protein Data Bank. The system aims to ease the growing burden on expert biocurators, who handled roughly 19,000 depositor messages across 8,000 entries in 2025. It combines a large language model with retrieval of relevant documentation to provide accurate, context-aware support.

papers.title: An evidence-weighted knowledge framework with path-aware reasoning for personalized lifestyle management in chronic disease.
papers.abstract: Healthy lifestyle management is essential for chronic disease prevention and long-term care. However, evidence linking lifestyle behaviors, biological mechanisms, and health outcomes is dispersed across diverse biomedical sources. This fragmentation makes it difficult for health professionals to efficiently retrieve and interpret evidence needed to inform personalized lifestyle guidance.
papers.summary: The authors propose an evidence-weighted knowledge framework that integrates fragmented biomedical evidence linking lifestyle behaviors, biological mechanisms, and health outcomes, using path-aware reasoning to support personalized lifestyle management for chronic disease. The framework aims to help health professionals more efficiently retrieve and interpret relevant evidence for tailored guidance. This is a conceptual/methodological proposal rather than a validated clinical tool.

papers.title: Multi-omics graph attention network reveals neuro-immune-tumor pathways in breast cancer liver depression syndrome.
papers.abstract: Liver depression syndrome (LDS) is a core Chinese medicine (CM) syndrome implicated in the onset and progression of breast cancer, whose molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering further investigation.
papers.summary: This study applies a multi-omics graph attention network to investigate the molecular mechanisms linking liver depression syndrome (LDS), a core Chinese medicine syndrome, to breast cancer progression. The approach integrates multiple omics layers to uncover neuro-immune-tumor pathways associated with LDS. The findings aim to bridge traditional Chinese medicine syndrome concepts with modern molecular network analysis.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that uses supervised contrastive learning to pretrain gene representations on a unified human-mouse shared gene space, then predicts transcription factor-target regulatory relationships from single-cell RNA-seq data. It models gene-cell expression via a multi-relational heterograph to address noise, sparsity, and cross-species distribution shifts in GRN inference.

papers.title: Radiomics and deep learning for immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes: imaging-derived immune phenotyping and clinical translation across solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of multiple solid tumors, but durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients and conventional size-based imaging does not fully capture immune-related response patterns. Radiomics and deep learning offer a route to convert routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT into quantitative biomarkers of tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and temporal treatment response. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence across solid tumors with an emphasis on four questions that are often separated in the literature: what
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on using radiomics and deep learning to predict immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes across solid tumors. It argues that routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT can be converted into quantitative imaging biomarkers of tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and treatment response, potentially enabling non-invasive 'imaging-derived immune phenotyping' to guide clinical decisions. The review emphasizes the need to integrate these imaging approaches with clinical translation across cancer types.

papers.title: Explainable growth stage classification of cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) leaves and key feature visualization using vision transformer and transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate and objective plant phenotyping is crucial for optimizing agricultural practices, understanding plant development, and enabling rapid responses to environmental changes. Traditional methods, often relying on visual observation, can be subjective, time-consuming, and may overlook subtle but important differences. This study demonstrates the power of combining digital imaging with deep learning to classify plant material with high accuracy, even when visual differences are minimal. We focused on differentiating between stage D (light green) and stage E (dark green) leaves of cacao (Theo
papers.summary: This study applies a vision transformer with transfer learning to classify cacao leaves into two visually similar developmental stages (D and E) based on digital images, achieving high accuracy where human visual inspection struggles. The authors also visualize key features driving the model's decisions, making the classification interpretable. The work demonstrates how deep learning can support objective, automated plant phenotyping in agriculture.

papers.title: Exploring the key genes of colorectal "adenoma-cancer" based on graph transformer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, and the precise identification of biomarkers from colonic adenoma to cancer is of great significance for preventing the development of adenocarcinoma. Given that existing methods inadequately capture the topological network relationships among genes, this study proposes a graph neural network model based on multifeature learning, named ChebTs, to investigate the correlation between key genes involved in the colorectal "adenoma-cancer" transition. The GSE41657 and GSE31905 datasets from the GEO database were stratified in
papers.summary: This study introduces ChebTs, a graph transformer-based neural network that integrates multiple gene features to identify key genes driving the transition from colorectal adenoma to cancer. Using GEO datasets GSE41657 and GSE31905, the model aims to better capture topological gene network relationships than prior methods, potentially improving biomarker discovery for early CRC prevention.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Stem Cell Research: From Biological Data to Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Stem cell (SC) research plays a central role in disease modeling and regenerative medicine, yet its clinical translation remains challenged by biological heterogeneity, incomplete cellular maturation, stringent quality-control requirements, and increasingly complex biological and clinical data. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful computational approach for extracting biologically meaningful information from these data, enabling quantitative characterization of SC behavior and predictive modeling across diverse experimental and translational applications. This review presents a unif
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across stem cell research, from analyzing complex biological data to supporting clinical translation. It highlights how ML helps address challenges like cellular heterogeneity, incomplete maturation, and quality control in regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Bio-Inspired Artificial Intelligence Multimorbidity Score for Human-Machine Clinical Risk Stratification.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity is strongly associated with mortality, but existing comorbidity indices often generalize poorly across populations because they depend on fixed disease lists and context-specific weights. We developed the large-language-model-based multimorbidity score (LLM-MMS), a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity phenotype score, as a bio-inspired artificial intelligence score for human-machine clinical risk stratification and evaluated it for all-cause mortality prediction in 770,439 adults from 9 international longitudinal cohorts. Harmonized participant-level data wer
papers.summary: The authors developed LLM-MMS, a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity score designed as a bio-inspired AI tool for clinical risk stratification. They evaluated its ability to predict all-cause mortality in 770,439 adults across 9 international longitudinal cohorts, aiming to overcome the poor generalizability of fixed disease-list comorbidity indices.
